subject: DPA: proof-of-erase schedule & backup handoff clarifications
messages:
From: Max Taylor <max.taylor@auroradata.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Questions on DPA: erase evidence & backup timeline

Irene —

Thanks again for the draft DPA. A few practical questions came up on our side as we prepare redlines:

1) Post-termination timeline: what exact windows will Redwood commit to for (a) deletion of production indexes and KV caches, (b) deletion of point-in-time backups/snapshots, and (c) removal of any onshore/offshore replicated copies?

2) Proof artifacts: what form will the certified "erase" evidence take? We need an auditable record that shows which objects were removed, timestamps, and a digest/hash for verification — ideally something we can ingest into our contract repository.

3) Onshore handoff: we have a legal requirement to collect an onshore-delivered manifest for EU customer data. Can Redwood support a handoff (SFTP or signed manifest) and a narrow onshore window?

4) Backup scope: do system-level forensic logs, telemetry snapshots, and debug traces fall under the same removal windows, or are they retained differently (e.g., 90/180-day debug retention)?

We have a procurement cutoff at the end of Nov, so an answer by next week would be great. I can loop in legal if needed.

Best,
Max
Max Taylor
Head of Cloud Security, Aurora Data
max.taylor@auroradata.com

-----Original Message-----

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Max Taylor <max.taylor@auroradata.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 11:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA: erase evidence & backup timeline

Hi Max —

Thanks for the clear list. Below is a practical proposal we typically provide to mid-enterprise customers; happy to tighten the windows for Aurora if you have a regulatory constraint.

Proposed Redwood standard windows (post-termination):
- Production indexes & runtime KV caches: deleted within 30 days; immediate tombstoning upon termination trigger, with asynchronous GC within 30 days.
- Point-in-time snapshots/backups: 90 days retention after termination trigger; scheduled snapshot purge at day 90.
- Long-term archival copies (only if configured): 180 days unless specifically requested to be retained longer; otherwise scheduled purge at day 180.
- Onshore replicas: removed as part of the above windows; where an onshore handoff is requested we can prioritize removal and provide a handoff manifest before purge.

Proof artifacts we can provide:
- A deletion manifest (CSV) listing object IDs, deletion timestamps, and SHA256 digest for each exported file.
- A deletion ticket ID from our ticketing system and a signed attest token (PGP-signed or KMS-signed) verifying the manifest hash.
- Audit logs showing the purge jobs and worker IDs involved (retained per our SOC2 retention schedule but cross-referenced in the manifest).

Operational notes:
- Backups that include debug traces/telemetry are handled separately: we mark them in the manifest and can segregate by tag (telemetry/debug vs. customer-data). Typical practice is 90 days for backups and 180 days for colder archives.
- Legal holds: any active legal hold will block automatic purge; we will provide notification and a snapshot of held objects.

Next steps: Marissa and Ben are on copy — Marissa, can you confirm whether the proposed form of proof (CSV manifest + signed hash + ticket reference) is acceptable from a legal/contract perspective? Ben, can you confirm we can support an SFTP onshore handoff and the timing constraints?

If that all works I can draft the DPA paragraph text and provide a sample manifest template.

Regards,
Irene Choi
Director, Trust & Compliance | Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com

-----On Thu, 12 Nov 2026 08:45:00 +0000, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com> wrote:-----

Max / Irene / Ben —

Thanks, Max — this is helpful. A couple of addenda from legal/ops attached (erase-evidence-matrix.xlsx and redline_dpa_proof_section.pdf). Key points: 

- Evidence format: we prefer a CSV manifest plus a PDF "manifest attestation" that includes the signed SHA256 digest and the ticket reference. That is usually sufficient for legal acceptance and audit ingestion.

- Acceptance window: Redwood will produce the manifest within 10 business days of the scheduled purge job; Aurora will have a 5-business-day review/acceptance window. If no objections are raised, Redwood will proceed with final purge and provide final attest.

- Onshore handoff: Ops can push the manifest to an Aurora-managed SFTP endpoint and, if required, provide a notarized attest via a signing authority. We will need the SFTP details and an IP allowlist prior to handoff.

- Backups & logs: we will tag backups that contain customer PII/PHI and include them in the manifest. Telemetry/debug traces will be shown separately; we can commit to removing PII-containing debug traces on the same 90-day schedule.

Ben — can you confirm the SFTP workflow (expected lead time for IP allowlist, any size constraints, and whether we should use an encrypted bundle vs. per-file manifests)?

Max — if you’re open, propose a 30-minute sync next week to walk through the matrix and get the SFTP endpoint. We can then deliver a redlined DPA paragraph and a sample manifest.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachments: erase-evidence-matrix.xlsx; redline_dpa_proof_section.pdf

-----On Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:12:00 +0000, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com> wrote:-----

All — quick ops note:

- SFTP handoff is supported. Typical onboarding timeline is 3 business days to add an IP allowlist + test account; larger manifests (>5GB) are transferred as encrypted bundles with accompanying per-file checksums.
- We can produce the deletion manifest as a per-job CSV with a signed SHA256 digest. For an onshore handoff we can also produce a PGP-signed bundle and provide the public key fingerprint in the manifest.
- If Aurora requires prioritized purge for onshore replicas, we can schedule an expedited purge window (target: within 10 business days) but this requires a scoped change request and an approval ticket.

Irene / Marissa: happy to include the expedited option explicitly in the DPA redline (timed by an approved service request ID).

Ben Carter
Sr. Manager, Ops Engineering | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

-----On Sun, 15 Nov 2026 14:03:00 +0000, Max Taylor <max.taylor@auroradata.com> wrote:-----

Irene / Marissa / Ben —

Thanks for the detail and the attachments. The proposed artifacts and acceptance window look acceptable to our legal team, with two asks:

1) We need an explicit onshore handoff clause (SFTP push + signed manifest) with a maximum delivery SLA of 10 business days post-scheduled purge.
2) We would like Redwood to include a statement confirming that PII-containing telemetry/debug traces will be included in the 90-day backup purge or else enumerated in the manifest as held items with reason.

If you can incorporate those clauses in the redline, we can move to signature — procurement is standing by and will start DocuSign once the DPA paragraph is in place. I’ll send the SFTP endpoint and an initial test user later today.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Max
